title: Minimum Cost to Merge Sorted Lists
summary: Given a 2D integer array where each sub-array is sorted in non-decreasing order, you must repeatedly choose two distinct sub-arrays, merge them, and remove the original sub-arrays.
statement: Given a 2D integer array where each sub-array is sorted in non-decreasing order, you must repeatedly choose two distinct sub-arrays, merge them, and remove the original sub-arrays. The cost to merge two sub-arrays is the sum of their lengths plus the absolute difference between their medians. Continue merging until only one sub-array remains. The task is to find the minimum total cost for this process. The median of a sorted array is the middle element, or the left middle element if the array has an even number of elements.
constraints: 2≤len(lists)≤12; every list is nonempty and sorted.
Merge cost is combined length plus the absolute difference of the two left-middle medians.
Repeatedly merge until one sorted list remains with minimum total cost.
hints: Every intermediate merged list corresponds only to a subset of original lists, regardless of merge order.
Precompute the sorted union, length, and left-middle median for every subset.
Subset DP splits each mask into two nonempty parts and adds their optimal costs plus the final merge cost.
The last merge of any merge tree partitions its leaves into two subsets, so considering every partition proves optimal substructure.
editorial: The last merge of any merge tree partitions its leaves into two subsets, so considering every partition proves optimal substructure.

tests.explanation: Merging the first two costs six, then merging with the third costs twelve, totaling eighteen.
The sole merge costs length two plus median difference two, totaling four.
